papers.abstract: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is driven by the constitutively active BCR::ABL1 kinase, which promotes uncontrolled cell proliferation. Although protein-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have revolutionized CML treatment, resistance remains a significant barrier to curative therapy, particularly due to BCR::ABL1 mutations and the persistence of leukemia stem cells (LSCs). New treatment strategies that directly inhibit BCR::ABL1 protein expression are needed to achieve more effective therapy. Using a high-content antibody microarray and bioinformatics analyses, we investigated differences in the proteome and phosphorylation landscape of Imatinib (IM)-resistant cells and identified highly activated members of the eukaryotic translation initiation complex (eIF4F), particularly eIF4G1, a core component of eIF4F. These eIF4F complex members are highly expressed and activated in CD34+ CML stem/progenitor cells and in IM-resistant cells. Genetic inhibition of eIF4G1 or pharmacological targeting with the small-molecule inhibitor SBI-756 diminished eIF4F complex assembly, reduced overall translation initiation, reduced BCR::ABL1 expression and key downstream targets, impaired the survival of nonresponder stem/progenitor cells, including BCR::ABL1-T315I mutant cells, and sensitized them to TKIs, with strong synergistic effects in vitro and in a PDX model. These findings underscore the potential of eIF4F complex inhibition as a new therapeutic strategy to overcome TKI resistance in CML and other BCR::ABL1+ malignancies.

papers.abstract: In Head and Neck Cancer (HNC), even short delays in treatment can worsen prognosis. We used real-world data to quantify waiting times and identify patient, tumour and health service factors associated with treatment delay in England. Using linked national datasets (Cancer Registry, Cancer Waiting Times, Hospital Episodes Statistics, Radiotherapy and Chemotherapy), we calculated waiting times from referral to first treatment (surgery or (chemo)radiation) and used multivariable logistic regression models to examine factors associated with delay. Of 30,506 patients, 43% experienced treatment delay ( > 62 days from referral). Long delays ( > 90 days) affected 11% of patients treated with primary surgery and 20% of those receiving primary (chemo)radiation. Non-urgent referral (30% of patients) was the strongest predictor of long delay (aOR 4.07, CI: 3.54-4.68). Additional risk-factors included initial assessment at non-specialist (spoke) hospitals, non-oropharyngeal cancers, and higher socio-economic deprivation. Treatment delays in HNC are worsening, particularly for patients treated with primary (chemo)radiation. Referral route is the strongest determinant. Interventions should focus on optimising referral pathways, increasing awareness of HNC symptoms among the public and primary care, and acknowledging the different drivers of delay associated with surgery and (chemo)radiation therapy.

papers.abstract: Evaluation of arterial resection (AR) during pancreatoduodenectomy (PD) remains limited. This study compares PD with AR to PD with venous resection (VR) and no vascular resection (NVR). Patient demographics, outcomes, and changes over 5 years are evaluated. In this study, NSQIP data was analyzed comparing patients undergoing PD with AR to NVR and VR. Demographics and 30-day post-operative outcomes were compared, and multivariable modeling evaluated factors associated with serious complications and mortality. Propensity score matched (PSM) analysis compared AR to NVR, AR to VR, and VR to NVR. We evaluated 28,083 patients with 4.1% having AR and 10.9% having VR. After demographic adjustment, both AR (1.40; p < 0.001) and VR (OR 1.32; p < 0.001) were independently associated with serious complications and mortality (AR: OR 2.03; p = 0.002; VR: OR 1.43; p = 0.043). PSM supported increased serious complications (+4.9% VR, p < 0.001; +5.40% AR, p = 0.008) but not mortality (+0.4% VR, p = 0.323; +1.4% AR, p = 0.067) compared to NVR. AR did not increase the risk of complications or mortality compared to VR following PSM. Evaluating AR/VR from 2017 to 2021 shows consistent demographics but increasing neoadjuvant treatment (40.2%-48.9%; p < 0.001). Length of stay has decreased (12.3-9.6 days; p < 0.001), while serious complications (19.7%-22.1%) and mortality (1.7%-3.1%) remained similar. Results demonstrate that arterial (and venous) resection during PD is independently associated with 30-day serious complications compared to without vascular resection. However, absolute morbidity rates during vascular resection may be acceptable in selected patients and appear to be similar with arterial and venous resection. Future studies evaluating long-term outcomes are needed.

papers.abstract: BRCAness, a phenotype associated with homologous recombination deficiency, has not been fully characterized in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) with residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC), especially regarding prognosis and regimen-specific postoperative management. We analyzed 137 patients with TNBC who had residual invasive disease after NAC. BRCAness status was assessed in surgical specimens using multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA). Its associations with clinicopathological features and survival were evaluated according to NAC regimen, and prognostic models for disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS) were developed by combining BRCAness with clinicopathological variables. BRCAness was identified in 42.3% of tumors and was associated with high histological grade, high Ki-67, and perineural invasion. Patients with BRCAness-positive tumors had worse survival than those with BRCAness-negative tumors (5-year DFS, 50.0% vs. 68.2%, p = 0.020; 5-year OS, 58.6% vs. 78.1%, p = 0.014). This prognostic effect was evident in patients treated with anthracycline-based NAC, but not in those treated with platinum-based regimens. Models incorporating BRCAness showed good discrimination (DFS C-index, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.62-0.78; OS C-index, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.69-0.81). Among BRCAness-positive patients who had received anthracycline-based NAC, adjuvant chemotherapy was associated with better survival (5-year DFS, 55.6% vs. 27.3%, p = 0.035; 5-year OS, 66.7% vs. 36.4%, p = 0.023). BRCAness was associated with poorer outcome in residual TNBC after NAC and may help identify patients with different prognoses and postoperative treatment patterns.

papers.abstract: Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) is associated with Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection in a subset of cases. We previously showed that the incidence of HL in Taiwan increased ~2.5-fold between 2001 and 2020, particularly among young women with the nodular sclerosis (NS) subtype. In this nationwide multicenter study, we evaluated EBV status in HL to determine its impact on clinicopathologic features and survival outcomes. We found that the proportion of EBV-associated HL in Taiwan declined over the past two decades, from 39% to 27%. EBV-positive frequency exhibited a bimodal age distribution, peaking in children 70 years (80%), with the lowest frequency in patients 20-29 years (11%). Compared with EBV-negative patients, EBV-positive patients were older (53.5 vs. 32.9 years; p 60 years), B symptoms, non-NS histology, EBV-positivity, advanced-stage disease (Stage III-IV), and a high International Prognostic Score (IPS, 4-7). On multivariate analysis, older age and a high IPS retained prognostic significance. Large registry datasets from Taiwan and the US further demonstrated that survival outcomes have improved over the past two decades. Female patients and those with the NS and nodular lymphocyte-predominant subtypes had significantly better survival. These findings provide insight into the biological impact of EBV in HL and help inform strategies for disease prevention and management.

papers.abstract: Since the discovery and application of green fluorescent protein for use as an optical tag, fluorescent proteins (FPs) have changed the way we observe biological signals and processes. FP and fluorescent biosensor design has continued to advance, facilitated by new technologies and developments in chemistry, physics, engineering and screening technologies. We summarize some of the recent developments in FP engineering, focusing on insights that have led to improved photostability or longer wavelengths, among other improvements, highlighting mScarlet as a case study. We also discuss the engineering of new fluorescent biosensors, focusing on the ways in which screening, quantitative imaging, spatial resolution and multiplexing have been improved in recent years. Finally, we conclude with a perspective on what the future holds for the next generation of FPs and biosensors.

papers.abstract: The parent body of the C-type asteroid Ryugu experienced aqueous alteration. The past aqueous environments have been reconstructed using mineralogies and geochemical modeling, often assuming Na-Cl-rich fluid compositions. Here, we reconstruct Ryugu's aqueous environment using chemical equilibrium modeling constrained by Electron Probe Microanalyzer (EPMA) and X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectroscopy. Our results suggest that Ryugu water possessed lower salinity than previously estimated and was highly reducing (Eh: -0.5 to -0.8 V) and strongly alkaline (pH: 10.3 to 11.5) conditions conducive to prebiotic organic reactions. The inferred high hydrogen fugacity, lack of NaCl, and low salinity recorded in Ryugu sample suggest that aqueous alteration occurred beneath a surface ice layer, with subsequent ice sublimation driving water loss. These findings refine our understanding of C-type asteroids evolution and the quantity and nature of water delivered to the early Earth.

papers.abstract: Our understanding of cell division control traditionally comes via using liquid broths or 2D flat-plate cultures - which cannot recapitulate the complex visco-elasto-plastic properties of natural habitats such as tissues, mucus, and soil. Consequently, how such regimes of physical confinement influence proliferative growth remains poorly understood. Here, using engineered, mechanically tunable and transparent growth matrices, we directly visualize yeast budding and division across 3D viscoelastic regimes. We discover that elevated physical confinement drastically prolongs budding intervals without any physiological defects or activating global regulatory programs. Remarkably, extended cell division times are not associated with transcriptional or proteomic signatures of mechanosensation or cell cycle regulation. Rather, 3D confinement physically constrains the volumetric growth of incipient buds - manifesting as delayed cell cycle progression. Hence, our findings establish that physical constrainment regulates eukaryotic cell division.

papers.abstract: Despite significant climate variability in the Northern Hemisphere ~50,000-12,000 years ago, the potential for vertebrates to periodically thrive in the glacial Arctic Ocean has been largely overlooked because ecosystem productivity was assumed to be too low. Here, we analyze fish otoliths preserved in deep-sea sediments and find that two Arctic endemic cod species, ice cod (Arctogadus glacialis) and polar cod (Boreogadus saida), lived at 87-89 °N ~ 48,000-35,000 years ago and reappeared at the onset of the Holocene ~12,000 years ago. A. glacialis also occurred north of Greenland at 84-85 °N ~ 20,000 years ago, during the peak of the Last Glacial Maximum, suggesting the presence of refugia that enabled survival and divergence from B. saida under the harshest climate conditions. These findings suggest that the glacial Arctic Ocean was not a barren ice desert but rather a breeding ground for the evolution of cold adaptation in marine fish.

papers.abstract: Understanding the functional consequences of genetic variants, particularly those classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS), is a major challenge in genomics. While variant effects at protein level are well recognized, roles in post-transcriptional regulation are increasingly appreciated. Here, we introduce cPRIME (prime editing with cDNA readout), a scalable method for assessing variant effects at RNA level. cPRIME employs prime editing to insert genetic variants into endogenous genomic loci, followed by the quantification of changes in variant frequencies at RNA (cDNA) and genomic DNA (gDNA) level. We demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse karyotypes and genomic loci and reveal that synonymous marker edits - frequently used in prime editing screens - can themselves alter RNA processing and thereby confound the interpretation of variant effects. Taken together, cPRIME provides a platform for studying the post-transcriptional consequences of genetic variants in their genomic context and establishes a framework for the functional interpretation of RNA-altering variants in cancer and other diseases.

papers.abstract: Intensive care unit-acquired pneumonia is often treated as a binary diagnosis, although clinical deterioration, imaging and microbial detection describe different aspects of disease. This Perspective proposes an explicit, graded and revisable assessment of whether a detected organism plausibly causes the current lung injury. The framework encompasses pneumonia arising during ventilation, pneumonia that precedes intubation and pneumonia in non-ventilated ICU patients. It places molecular results within clinical, anatomical, microbiological and host context and uses formal reassessment at 48-72 hours to guide treatment continuation, narrowing or discontinuation.

papers.abstract: To assess whether the association between postoperative diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and neurological worsening after eloquent-area glioma surgery differs according to lesion morphology. We retrospectively analyzed 139 consecutive patients undergoing resection of eloquent-area supratentorial gliomas (WHO 2-4). Postoperative MRI (< 48 h) classified lesions as sector- or rim-shaped. Neurological status was assessed at discharge and 4-6 months. DWI lesions occurred in 44/139 patients (31.7%; 31 sector-shaped, 13 rim-shaped); 59 (42.4%) worsened at discharge. Overall, DWI positivity alone was not associated with worsening. Sector-shaped DWI lesions were associated with neurological worsening (positive predictive value, PPV of 58.1%) and remained associated after multivariable adjustment (OR 3.83, 95% CI 1.30-11.29), although the confidence interval was wide and the unadjusted association was borderline. Rim-shaped lesions carried a PPV of 38.5%, comparable to the risk in DWI-negative patients (37.9%), and the two morphologies did not differ significantly in direct comparison. Awake craniotomy was also independently associated with worsening, and frontal site with a lower risk. 61% of worsening occurred with negative DWI. A deficit was present at the 4-6 month follow-up in 9 patients (6.5%), all with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, and was associated with a ≥ 50% evoked-potential decrease. In this cohort, postoperative DWI positivity was associated with neurological worsening mainly when the lesion was sector-shaped, a finding that requires confirmation in larger series. Rim-shaped lesions showed a risk of worsening similar to that of a negative scan. Most worsening occurs without DWI ischemia, suggesting non-ischemic mechanisms of function-guided surgery. A deficit at follow-up occurred only in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma and was associated with intraoperative neurophysiological changes.

papers.abstract: Missed genetic deletions can prevent cancer patients from receiving effective targeted therapy. Standard pipelines, such as TSO500, use bin count averaging for copy number variation detection but often overlook focal events. To address this, we developed a machine learning (ML) pipeline for deletion detection and zygosity evaluation within the MASTERsg precision oncology program. We focused on the tumor suppressor gene PTEN, whose loss confers sensitivity to mTOR/Akt inhibition. An Extreme Gradient Boosting model trained on PTEN-deleted and wild-type tumor samples identified focal deletions missed by the TSO500 pipeline and CNVkit that were associated with concordant PTEN protein loss by immunohistochemistry. Importantly, the model detected PTEN deletions in 33/204 profiled samples that were classified as PTEN wild-type by TSO500; 75% (15/20) of stainable cases showed absent or reduced PTEN protein expression. These findings demonstrate the potential of ML to enhance panel sequencing, uncovering therapeutically relevant alterations missed by established diagnostic methods.

papers.abstract: Therapeutic efficacy of temozolomide (TMZ) remains limited, and GBM patients generally experience poor outcomes due to the presence of multiple mechanisms of TMZ resistance. Previously, we developed two novel compounds: EPIC-1027, which targets HOTAIR/PRC2 complex, and EPIC-1042, which disrupts interaction between PTRF and CAV1. In this study, we aim to establish a novel combinatorial strategy for GBM by targeting mitochondrial function. Proteomics was employed to evaluate global protein alterations induced by EPIC-1027 and EPIC-1042. Super-resolution microscopy and transmission electron microscopy were used to characterize changes in mitochondrial morphology. Metabolic flux analysis was performed to assess alterations in cellular energy metabolism following combined treatment. An intracranial GBM model was established to validate the anti-GBM efficacy of EPIC-1027 and EPIC-1042 in vivo. Combined treatment with EPIC-1027 and EPIC-1042 reduced the abundance of respiratory chain complex proteins by promoting p62-dependent protein degradation, resulting in severe mitochondrial damage. Both glycolytic activity and oxidative phosphorylation were markedly suppressed following EPIC-1027 and EPIC-1042 treatment. In vitro, EPIC-1027 and EPIC-1042 exerted a synergistic inhibitory effect on GBM cell proliferation and significantly induced apoptosis in an MGMT-independent manner. In vivo, combined treatment with EPIC-1027 and EPIC-1042 significantly attenuated tumor growth and prolonged survival in mice bearing orthotopic GBM. Our study demonstrates that combined treatment with EPIC-1027 and EPIC-1042 induces mitochondrial structural abnormalities and functional impairment, leading to suppressed proliferation and enhanced apoptosis. These findings identified a novel combinatorial therapeutic strategy targeting mitochondria for the treatment of glioblastoma.

papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy has achieved clinical progress in various malignancies, yet primary and acquired resistance limits its efficacy in solid tumors. Myeloid cells in the tumor microenvironment (TME), including tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs), and myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), undergo metabolic reprogramming under hypoxia and nutrient stress. They impair effector T cell function and may contribute to exhaustion-associated states via nutrient competition, release of toxic metabolites, and formation of physical barriers, representing a critical resistance mechanism. This review summarizes the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of myeloid cells and the metabolic networks underlying their immunosuppressive phenotypes, focusing on dysregulated lipid and cholesterol metabolism, amino acid remodeling, the glycolytic switch, and subcellular stress responses. We analyze how metabolic dysregulation causes T cell dysfunction and, in defined contexts, contributes to exhaustion-associated transcriptional programs through nutrient competition, toxic metabolite accumulation, and upregulation of inhibitory receptor ligands, and summarize intervention strategies targeting myeloid recruitment, phenotypic remodeling, metabolic reprogramming, and pathological structures combined with ICB. We discuss challenges of efficacy heterogeneity and safety in clinical translation, and highlight the prospects of multi-omics and computational biology in guiding next-generation combination immunotherapy. Understanding myeloid metabolic plasticity may provide a basis for overcoming immunotherapy resistance and establishing precise synergistic strategies.

papers.title: Targeting myeloid cell plasticity and metabolic reprogramming to alleviate T cell dysfunction and exhaustion-associated states and enhance immune checkpoint blockade therapy.

papers.abstract: Persistent CAR-T donor cells after CAR-T-bridged allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) may complicate hematopoietic recovery. When CAR-T and HSCT cells share the same donor, standard donor chimerism cannot distinguish their contributions. We report three patients with relapsed/refractory T-cell malignancies who received CAR-T and allo-HSCT from distinct donors, enabling three-party short tandem repeat (STR) analysis to resolve CAR-T donor, HSCT donor, and recipient compartments. Patient 2, with detectable residual CAR transgene at transplantation (240 copies/µg gDNA), developed mixed chimerism with cytopenia (MCC) and a CAR-T donor contribution of 47.72%. Patient 3, also with detectable residual CAR transgene (22,162 copies/µg gDNA), developed mixed chimerism, with a CAR-T donor contribution of 14.23%. In contrast, Patient 1, with undetectable CAR transgene at transplantation, showed stable complete donor chimerism (CDC) and hematopoietic recovery. Guided by the two-step reconstitution pattern observed in Patient 1, we administered CAR-target-knockout donor lymphocyte infusion (KO-DLI) as rescue treatment in Patient 2 and preemptive intervention in Patient 3. Both eventually became CAR-undetectable, with restoration of CDC and hematologic recovery, although the independent effect of KO-DLI could not be isolated. All three remain in complete remission (follow-up + 713, +335, + 201 days). Residual CAR transgene at transplantation may serve as an early risk signal for CAR-T donor cell persistence, and KO-DLI warrants prospective validation as a transplantation-sparing salvage approach.

papers.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are key regulators of tumor progression and immune suppression within the tumor microenvironment (TME). Emerging evidence identifies ubiquitination, a dynamic post-translational modification that regulates protein stability, localization, and signaling activity, as a critical determinant of TAM function. Ubiquitin signaling orchestrates macrophage inflammatory responses, metabolic reprogramming, and tumor cell-immune cell crosstalk through coordinated actions of ubiquitin-activating enzymes, ubiquitin-conjugating enzymes, ubiquitin-protein ligases (E3s), and deubiquitinating enzymes (DUBs). Dysregulation of these ubiquitin networks fosters an immunosuppressive microenvironment, thereby promoting tumor growth, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance. In this review, we summarize recent advances in the role of ubiquitination in TAM biology, focusing on key E3 ubiquitin ligases and DUBs in TAM immunity. We further discuss emerging ubiquitin-dependent signaling pathways that integrate metabolic and inflammatory cues within TAMs. Finally, we highlight the therapeutic potential of targeting ubiquitination machinery to reprogram TAMs and remodel the TME. Collectively, this review provides a comprehensive framework for understanding ubiquitin-mediated regulation of TAM function and offers novel perspectives for developing ubiquitination-based cancer immunotherapies.

papers.abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) of histone H3 at lysine 9 (H3K9) contribute to chromatin homeostasis and transcriptional regulation and have been implicated in cancer progression. However, how distinct H3K9 modification states differ in function, compete for the same lysine residue, and dynamically respond to cellular context remains incompletely understood. This review summarizes the biochemical characteristics and enzymatic regulation of H3K9 methylation, acetylation, and non-acetyl acylations, including lactylation, β-hydroxybutyrylation, butyrylation, and crotonylation. We examine their roles in DNA replication, transcription, and DNA damage repair, as well as their interplay with other epigenetic regulatory mechanisms. We further discuss how H3K9-associated regulatory networks contribute to tumor proliferation, stemness maintenance, metabolic reprogramming, invasion and metastasis, immune microenvironment remodeling, therapeutic resistance, and programmed cell death, emphasizing their context-dependent and, in some settings, opposing biological effects. Finally, we evaluate preclinical and clinical advances in pharmacologically targeting H3K9-associated regulatory enzymes, distinguishing residue-specific mechanistic evidence from broader enzyme-level effects, and outline future directions for biomarker-guided epigenetic therapies in cancer.

papers.abstract: The intratumoral microbiome critically influences immunotherapy efficacy by modulating the host immune microenvironment and epigenetic landscape through its metabolites. Microbial derived metabolites such as short chain fatty acids, secondary bile acids, trimethylamine N oxide, and tryptophan derivatives reprogram host cell epigenetics via DNA methylation, histone modifications, and non-coding RNAs, thereby shaping anti-tumor immunity and driving either immune activation or resistance. In turn, the hypoxic, acidic, and nutrient deprived tumor microenvironment reshapes microbial composition and metabolism, forming a vicious cycle that further affects therapeutic outcomes. Given these pivotal roles, targeting the intratumoral microbiota has emerged as a promising strategy. Advances in synthetic biology have enabled the development of engineered bacteria as programmable living therapeutics. These engineered strains achieve tumor specific colonization, controlled drug release, and multimodal functions such as cytokine secretion, immune checkpoint blockade, STING pathway activation, and metabolic reprogramming. By enhancing immune checkpoint inhibitor efficacy and synergizing with cell therapies, engineered bacterial therapy represents a highly promising approach to improve immunotherapy efficiency. Despite challenges in clinical translation including heterogeneity, anti-vector immunity, and manufacturing complexity, this strategy offers a new paradigm for precision cancer treatment.

papers.abstract: AXL is a membrane-accessible receptor tyrosine kinase and a potential antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) target, but its therapeutic relevance in soft-tissue sarcoma remains incompletely defined. We evaluated the AXL-directed pyrrolobenzodiazepine ADC ADCT-601/mipasetamab uzoptirine using a sarcoma tissue microarray, patient-derived cell lines, and patient-derived xenografts. AXL expression was broad but heterogeneous, with the highest histotype-level expression in myxofibrosarcoma and undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma. In the patient-linked tissue-microarray cohort, AXL H-score was not associated with metastasis-free or overall survival after clinicopathologic adjustment. ADCT-601 was substantially more potent than a non-targeting anti-gp120 control ADC carrying the same SG3199-containing payload. Free-payload sensitivity varied between cell lines, indicating that intrinsic payload susceptibility contributes to activity, while the payload-matched comparison supports an additional effect of AXL-mediated delivery. ADCT-601 induced cell-cycle perturbation, apoptosis, and γ-H2AX accumulation. Combination experiments identified enhanced activity with DNA damage-response inhibition, particularly ATR inhibition, and in vivo studies supported antitumor activity in two sarcoma xenograft models. These data support biomarker-enriched development of next-generation AXL-directed ADC strategies while emphasizing antigen heterogeneity and therapeutic-index optimization.

papers.abstract: D2C7-ATC is a recombinant antibody-toxin conjugate (ATC) targeting wild-type epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and mutant EGFR variant III (EGFRvIII). We conducted a single-arm, single-site, open-label phase 1 trial evaluating a single infusion of D2C7-ATC via convection-enhanced delivery in the enhancing disease of 81 patients with biopsy-confirmed recurrent malignant glioma. The primary objective was to determine toxicity and the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) of D2C7-ATC. Secondary objectives included describing overall survival (OS) and assessing the association between EGFR expression and OS. The median overall survival (mOS) was 7.9 months among 72 patients with isocitrate dehydrogenase wild-type recurrent glioblastoma (IDHwt rGBM), including 35 patients in the dose-escalation stage (40 to 35,032 ng ml-1) and 37 patients in the dose-expansion stage (RP2D of 6,920 ng ml-1). D2C7-ATC was generally well tolerated, with mainly grade 1-2 treatment-related adverse events (67%). The maximum tolerated dose was exceeded at 35,032 ng ml-1, where four patients experienced dose-limiting toxicities, including grade 4 (N = 2) and grade 3 (N = 2) events. Eight patients died on trial; all deaths were unrelated to D2C7-ATC. Univariate analyses identified survival-associated biomarkers, including tumor D2C7 antibody reactivity, circulating cytokines, a tumor inflammatory gene signature and neutrophils, monocytes and lymphocytes in blood. Notably, patients with IDHwt rGBM with a D2C7 antibody reactivity score of <1.5+ in pre-treatment tumor had an mOS of 17.38 months, whereas those with low IL-8 in post-treatment plasma had an mOS of 16.6 months. These findings indicate that EGFR-targeted D2C7-ATC therapy prolongs survival in a subset of patients with IDHwt rGBM via intratumoral and systemic immune activation. papers.abstract: Here we present AmpliconSuite, a toolkit for focal amplification analysis from cancer whole-genome sequencing that identifies extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA), breakage-fusion-bridges and other amplification modes. Its ecContext module categorizes ecDNA structures to understand formation mechanisms. Validation across 175 metaphase fluorescence in situ hybridization-probed genes in 72 models demonstrated accurate predictions. Analysis of 6,506 patient pan-cancer samples revealed ecDNA-mediated oncogene co-amplification preferences. To democratize data sharing, we created AmpliconRepository, a community-contributable platform, enabling investigation of results across >15,000 publicly hosted samples.

papers.abstract: Prostate cancer is a common malignancy with a heterogeneous disease course. Prior studies have identified a paucity of point mutations in protein-coding genes and only a few clinically relevant driver alterations. Here, using the Pan Prostate Cancer Group whole genome sequencing dataset from 1001 men, we perform an integrative analysis of cancer driver genes by quantifying recurrent genomic alterations among small mutations, structural variants, and copy number alterations in 961 primary prostate tumour samples. We identify at least one recurrent somatic or germline alteration in 97% of tumours and identify putative driver genes and mechanisms of dysregulation including frequently altered regulatory elements. A prominent example is the activation of oncogenes by structural variation-mediated hijacking of onco-enhancers of the solute carrier gene family including SLC30A4. Other recurrent alterations including FOXA1, MDM4, COL5A1, TP53, and BRCA1 stratify with metastatic disease, with additional drivers enriched in African-ancestry tumours. One quarter of tumours have acquired genome-informed therapeutic targets. Unsupervised analysis of alterations reveals four oncotypes with distinct genetic and clinical characteristics, including two clinically unfavourable oncotypes with shorter metastasis-free survival. Our study uncovers the full spectrum and recurrence patterns of genomic driver alterations in primary prostate cancers and delivers targets for biomarker development, mechanistic studies, and potential therapeutic interventions.

papers.abstract: Prenatal maternal depression may have intergenerational effects on offspring brain development, with potential socioemotional consequences. This observational follow-up study examines brain development and subsequent negative emotionality among 109 infants born to mothers participating in a randomized clinical trial (NCT03011801). In the prior trial, brief interpersonal psychotherapy significantly reduced prenatal depression symptoms and disorder as the published primary and secondary endpoints. Exploratory infant outcomes include hippocampal and amygdala volumes at 6 weeks and negative emotionality at 6 months. Here we show that infants of mothers randomized to interpersonal psychotherapy during pregnancy have lower right hippocampal volume than infants of mothers in the enhanced usual care group (p = .002, d = 0.62). No statistically significant group differences are observed in left hippocampal or amygdala volume. Smaller hippocampal volume predicts subsequent lower negative emotionality (r = 0.19, p = 0.045). In this study, a maternal prenatal depression intervention is associated with differences in infant brain development with implications for their subsequent emotional health.

papers.abstract: High-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (HR-MDS) are associated with poor survival despite standard therapy with hypomethylating agents (HMAs). Although the VERONA trial did not meet its primary endpoint, a granular interpretation of these results alongside real-life data may help identify patient subsets that could potentially benefit. At the 2025 American Society of Hematology (ASH) Meeting and at the 2026 European Hematology Association Congress (EHA), several studies reported updated data on venetoclax-based combinations in HR-MDS across clinical and biological subgroups. The randomized phase III VERONA study evaluated venetoclax plus azacitidine (VEN/HMA) versus azacitidine alone in the frontline setting, while additional phase I/II and real-life studies explored oral hypomethylating backbones, therapy-related disease, and molecularly defined subsets. Collectively, these data suggest that venetoclax enhances response rates in HR-MDS, although survival benefits remain heterogeneous, with a potential benefit observed when used as a bridge to transplantation. Given the lack of randomized data in transplant-eligible patients, this Correspondence provides a narrative, non-systematic review of the available evidence based mostly on abstracts and not peer reviewed publications. Additionally, we summarize the most clinically relevant findings and discuss their implications for future treatment strategies.

papers.abstract: Attenuated oncolytic bacteria represent a promising targeted delivery platform for cancer therapy; however, the lack of non-invasive biomarkers to monitor their persistent intra-tumoral colonization severely limits clinical translation, efficacy assessment, and safety monitoring. Here, we identify the sustained elevation of peripheral blood CXCL1 as a dynamic, non-invasive biomarker for the persistent colonization of attenuated Salmonella in solid tumors. Across four orthotopic preclinical models (including lung, breast, and bladder cancers, as well as melanoma), effective bacterial colonization specifically drove prolonged systemic CXCL1 elevation. Focusing specifically on the melanoma model, rapid bacterial eradication via intratumoral antibiotics restored CXCL1 to baseline. Furthermore, comparisons with a colonization-deficient mutant strain confirmed that CXCL1 elevation strictly depends on intra-tumoral, rather than systemic, bacterial burden. Mechanistically, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) revealed that tumor-colonizing bacteria profoundly reshape the tumor microenvironment by directly activating and recruiting neutrophils, monocytes, and cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), which act as the primary cellular sources of CXCL1 production and systemic leakage. These findings highlight peripheral blood CXCL1 as a robust and actionable biomarker for real-time monitoring of oncolytic bacterial colonization, providing crucial guidance for dosing optimization and biosafety evaluation in clinical applications.

papers.abstract: Cancer progression does not occur in isolation: malignant-cell states and fates are shaped by specialized microenvironments, or cancer niches. Within primary tumors, vascular, stromal, immune and neural interactions create local hypoxic, metabolic and mechanical conditions that together influence malignant-cell behavior. These local environments sustain stem-like states, regulate immune surveillance and vascular remodeling, and influence dissemination and treatment response. Tumor-derived extracellular vesicles and other systemic signals connect primary tumors to distant organs, conditioning tissues before tumor-cell arrival and subsequently modulating disseminated tumor-cell seeding, dormancy, reactivation and outgrowth. Cancer niches therefore operate across spatial scales and disease stages, shaping tumor behavior in ways that cannot be explained by tumor-cell-intrinsic properties alone. Advances in single-cell and spatial profiling, organoid systems and intravital imaging are revealing their cellular composition, local architecture and evolution. In this review, we integrate primary, pre-metastatic and metastatic niche biology, examine how local environments evolve and influence one another during cancer progression, compare organ-specific metastatic niches and assess emerging therapeutic strategies. Effective niche-directed therapy will require identifying the interactions that sustain disease, showing that treatment disrupts them and determining which patients are most likely to benefit. Greater spatial, temporal and functional resolution may reveal new therapeutic vulnerabilities and create opportunities to prevent relapse and achieve more durable disease control.

papers.abstract: The rapidly global deployment of COVID-19 mRNA-LNP vaccines established the clinical feasibility of combining RNA medicine with LNP delivery systems, transforming a long-standing experimental concept into a scalable therapeutic modality, previously considered impossible. Currently, the value of mRNA-LNPs has been expanding from infectious disease vaccines to cancer immunotherapy, personalized neoantigen vaccination, in vivo immune-cell engineering, protein replacement therapy, mRNA-encoded biologics and genome editing, with particular relevance to hematology and oncology. However, in hematologic and oncologic settings, therapeutic success is constrained by biological barriers that less prominent in prophylactic vaccination. Systemically administered LNPs are strongly influenced by hepatic sequestration, protein corona formation and mononuclear-phagocyte clearance; solid tumors additionally present heterogeneous vasculature, variable enhanced permeability and retention, dense extracellular matrix, elevated interstitial pressure and limited intratumoral diffusion. Hematologic applications face a different set of constraints, including access to spleen and bone marrow, selective delivery to T cells, NK cells and hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), and preservation of the normal marrow niche. In this Review, we therefore discuss the molecular and principles of formulation that underpin mRNA-LNP performance in hematology and oncology, including mRNA engineering, lipid nanoparticle architecture, intracellular trafficking and selective organ targeting(SORT) delivery strategies, oncology applications spanning neoantigen vaccines, tumor-microenvironment reprogramming, mRNA-encoded biologics, gene editing and combination therapy; and hematology applications including in vivo CAR-T, CAR-NK and HSPC engineering. We further consider how inefficient extrahepatic delivery, limited endosomal escape, context-dependent reactogenicity, repeat-dosing constraints and the manufacturing complexity of individualized products continue to limit broader clinical translation. Emerging strategies, including artificial-intelligence-guided RNA and lipid design, self-amplifying RNA, circular RNA and next-generation thermostable formulations, may help address these application limitations in the fields of hematology and oncology.

papers.abstract: Over recent years, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy has markedly improved outcomes for patients with relapsed or refractory hematological malignancies. Nevertheless, a substantial proportion of patients still experience relapse or progression after treatment, driven by factors including antigen escape, suboptimal CAR-T cell expansion and persistence, functional exhaustion, and remodeling of the tumor microenvironment. In the context of managing patients who fail initial CAR-T therapy, CAR-T-centered sequential therapy has been increasingly investigated as a potential therapeutic approach. The selection of therapeutic targets and treatment approaches may be informed by resistance mechanisms, changes in target antigen expression, and disease progression patterns following prior treatment, with the aim of prolonging disease control and improving long-term outcomes. This review summarizes recent progress in CAR-T-centered sequential therapy, with particular emphasis on same-target retreatment, switching to different antigens, multi-target stepwise CAR-T regimens, and the sequential integration of CAR-T with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, radiotherapy, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and other immunomodulatory approaches. We further discuss the biological rationale and clinical settings of these CAR-T-centered sequential approaches in the context of antigen escape, CAR-T cell functional decline, tumor clonal evolution, and immune microenvironment remodeling. Additionally, we discuss factors that may inform the selection of subsequent regimens, including the initial treatment response, antigen status at relapse, CAR-T cell persistence, and the patient's therapeutic window, as well as the clinical settings in which these sequential approaches have been explored.

papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated substantial weight reduction and cardiometabolic benefit in randomized trials; however, prospective implementation evidence from digital care models and female sex community populations remains limited. Here we report outcomes from an observational study of 8,127 women initiating GLP-1RA therapy (99.8% tirzepatide) through a structured digital program incorporating mandatory biochemical monitoring, weekly video-supported follow-up and clinician-guided dose titration in the UK. Mean weight reduction was 16.1 kg (95% confidence interval 15.9 to 16.2; P < 0.001), representing 15.5% of baseline weight; 83.1% achieved ≥10% and 22.4% achieved ≥20% weight loss, with consistent responses across age, baseline weight and socioeconomic strata. Among participants with paired biomarker data, mean glycated hemoglobin decreased by 3.3 mmol mol-1 (95% confidence interval 3.1 to 3.4; P < 0.001), normalizing in 84.5% of those with baseline diabetes-range values and 96.3% with prediabetes, and lipid parameters improved significantly (reductions in total cholesterol of 0.77 mmol l-1, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol of 0.61 mmol l-1 and triglycerides of 0.47 mmol l-1). Retention was 91.4% at 6 months, with no serious treatment-related adverse events. These findings support the feasibility of delivering structured, digitally enabled obesity pharmacotherapy at scale and provide prospective real-world implementation evidence for this care model. Interpretation is limited by the observational design, absence of a comparator group, self-pay population and 6-month follow-up.

papers.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the most common form of lung cancer and is often diagnosed at an advanced stage, leading to poor prognosis. Carcinoembryonic antigen-related cell adhesion molecule 5 (CEACAM5) has emerged as a potential biomarker in colorectal and other gastrointestinal cancer; however, its role in NSCLC remains unexplored. This study evaluated the prognostic role of the CEACAM5 biomarker in metastatic non-squamous (mNSQ) NSCLC using real-world data. CEACAM5 expression was assessed via immunohistochemistry of archival tissue from 336 eligible patients. Real-world overall survival (rwOS) was the primary outcome analyzed across six treatment cohorts. Secondary outcomes included prevalence of CEACAM5 expression (high, moderate, negative) by cohort and tumor site (primary vs. metastatic) and other outcomes including real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS), time to next treatment (rwTTNT), and time to treatment discontinuation (rwTTD). High CEACAM5 expression was observed in approximately 18% of the overall population, with consistent levels observed across both primary and metastatic tumor samples. No significant associations were found between different CEACAM5 expression levels and rwOS, rwPFS, rwTTNT, and rwTTD, across all cohorts. CEACAM5 did not demonstrate prognostic value in this retrospective cohort study of patients with metastatic NSCLC. Further research to confirm our findings is needed.

papers.abstract: Thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are rare thoracic malignancies for which racial disparities in outcomes remain poorly characterized. We evaluated survival outcomes across racial groups and explored the clinical and sociodemographic factors that may help contextualize any observed differences. We retrospectively analyzed 128 consecutive patients with histologically confirmed TETs referred to the University of Chicago between January 1989 and March 2024. Associations between race, socioeconomic variables, and overall survival (OS) were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression, Cox proportional hazards models, and inverse probability of treatment weighting with average treatment effect (IPTW-ATE). Among 128 patients (75 White, 58%; 31 Black, 24%), Black race showed numerically worse OS on univariable analysis (hazard ratios [HR] 1.90, 95% confidence intervals [CI] 0.93-3.88; P = .077). Socioeconomic disparities were substantial: 74.2% of Black patients resided in low-income areas versus 12.2% of White patients (adjusted odds ratio 4.45, 95% CI 2.60-7.64; P < .0001). On multivariable analysis, thymic carcinoma histology (HR 3.97; P = .0012) and age older than 60 years (HR 2.19; P = .032) independently predicted worse survival. Black patients demonstrated numerically poorer OS (HR 2.49; P = .098). After IPTW-ATE adjustment, the association between Black race and OS was attenuated (HR 1.66, 95% CI 0.82-3.33; P = .157). Socioeconomic disadvantage emerged as one of several factors that may help contextualize the observed survival disparities in TETs. The attenuation of the effect estimates after adjustment for area-level socioeconomic factors suggests that social determinants of health may be relevant to the interpretation of these findings. Larger multi-institutional studies are needed to validate these observations.

papers.abstract: Hypochloremia is associated with poor prognosis in various malignant tumors. However, longitudinal trajectories of serum chloride in cancer patients and their relationship with mortality remain unexplored. This study aimed to delineate dynamic serum chloride trajectory patterns and analyze their association with mortality in patients with malignancies. This retrospective cohort study included 4,115 patients with malignant tumors from the MIMIC-IV database who had serial serum chloride measurements within the first 5 days of ICU admission, plus an additional 518 patients from Zibo Municipal Hospital for external validation. We applied group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) to stratify patients into three distinct serum chloride trajectory classes. The primary outcomes were 28-day and 365-day all-cause mortality, which were assessed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were further conducted to verify the robustness of the study findings. Three distinct serum chloride trajectory patterns were identified in both the MIMIC-IV primary cohort and the external validation cohort: Class 1 (initial hyperchloremia resolving to normal levels), Class 2 (persistent normochloremia), and Class 3 (progressive hyperchloremia). In the fully adjusted Cox regression model (Model 3), Class 3 was an independent predictor of 28-day (HR = 1.55, 95% CI: 1.26-1.92) and 365-day all-cause mortality (HR = 1.38, 95%CI: 1.19-1.60) in the MIMIC-IV cohort. This prognostic value was validated in the external validation cohort, where Class 3 was also associated with a significantly increased 28-day mortality risk (HR = 1.90, 95%CI: 1.08-3.33). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis revealed that Class 3 patients had significantly lower survival rates at both 28-day and 365-day follow-ups. Subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses further verified the robustness of the association between progressive hyperchloremia and adverse mortality outcomes. Progressive hyperchloremia trajectory independently predicts early and late mortality in cancer patients, and may offer a dynamic, low-cost biomarker for risk stratification.

papers.abstract: Although bladder cancer mortality has modestly declined in the United States, co-occurring substance use disorders (SUDs) may contribute to adverse outcomes and widening health disparities among affected individuals. This study evaluated temporal trends in mortality involving both bladder cancer and SUDs in the United States between 1999 and 2023. Mortality data related to patients aged ≥25 were obtained from the CDC WONDER Database. Deaths involving bladder cancer were identified using ICD-10 code C67 in combination with ICD-10 codes F10-F19 for substance use disorders listed among multiple causes of death. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 population were calculated and Joinpoint regression was used to estimate annual percent changes (APCs) and average annual percent changes (AAPCs). Between 1999 and 2023, 63,258 deaths involving both bladder cancer and SUDs were identified. Overall, the AAMR increased significantly at an annual average percentage change (AAPC) of 13.38% (95% CI: 10.69-16.14). Males had a substantially higher mortality burden than females (50,299 vs 12,959). White individuals and adults aged ≥85 were accounted for the largest mortality burden. Mortality rates were consistently higher in nonmetropolitan populations and increased across all U.S. census regions. Mortality involving bladder cancer and coexisting SUDs increased over time and mirrored broader national substance-related mortality trends. These findings support integrated oncology- and addiction-focused care approaches, as well as public health strategies aimed at improving access to cancer care, addiction treatment, and rural health services.

papers.abstract: Atypical spindle cell lipomatous tumor (ASCLT) is a rare benign adipocytic neoplasm, and primary involvement of the retroperitoneum is exceedingly uncommon. Because its imaging features overlap with those of other fat-containing tumors, particularly atypical lipomatous tumor/well-differentiated liposarcoma (ALT/WDL), preoperative diagnosis remains challenging. We report a case of primary retroperitoneal ASCLT in a 58-year-old woman whose lesion was incidentally detected during a routine physical examination. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a small, well-defined fat-containing mass located between the celiac trunk and the superior mesenteric artery, with fat-related signal attenuation on fat-suppressed sequences, no obvious diffusion restriction, and mild reticular enhancement after contrast administration. Complete surgical excision was performed, and postoperative histopathological, immunohistochemical, and molecular findings supported the diagnosis of ASCLT, with no MDM2 amplification. Compared with previously reported retroperitoneal ASCLT cases, the present case provides detailed CT and multiparametric MRI findings for a small, incidentally detected lesion adjacent to major abdominal vessels. Recognition of this imaging pattern may help include ASCLT in the preoperative differential diagnosis and support appropriate surgical planning, while definitive diagnosis still requires pathological and molecular confirmation.

papers.abstract: Pulmonary carcinoid tumorlets are small (< 5 mm) neuroendocrine proliferations that are usually identified incidentally in resected lung tissue. Their coexistence with a spatially separate lung adenocarcinoma is uncommon and may complicate the interpretation of multiple pulmonary nodules. A 71-year-old woman with multiple bilateral pulmonary micronodules that had remained radiologically stable for approximately 2 years was admitted after a newly detected lesion in the apicoposterior segment of the left upper lobe was considered suspicious for lung cancer. She reported occasional chest tightness and intermittent cough with sputum and had never smoked. Bronchoscopy and brush cytology were negative. The patient underwent video-assisted thoracoscopic wedge resection of the left upper lobe lesion. Frozen-section examination showed adenocarcinoma, prompting a left upper lobectomy with systematic lymph-node dissection. A left lower lobe wedge resection was performed to sample representative micronodules. Final pathology showed a 3.0-cm invasive adenocarcinoma (approximately 80% acinar and 20% lepidic patterns), without visceral pleural, definite vascular invasion, or metastasis in 17 sampled lymph nodes (pT1cN0M0, stage IA3). The left lower lobe nodules were reported as pulmonary carcinoid tumorlets and were positive for AE1/AE3, synaptophysin, chromogranin A, CD56, and TTF-1, with a Ki-67 index of approximately 2%. The adenocarcinoma harbored an EGFR exon 21 L858R mutation. She was discharged 1 week after surgery. This case illustrates that pulmonary micronodules accompanying a dominant lung cancer may represent a separate neuroendocrine proliferation rather than intrapulmonary metastases. Diagnosis requires correlation of lesion size, morphology, and immunophenotype. Unsampled contralateral nodules could remain radiologically indeterminate and undergo structured surveillance.

papers.abstract: To evaluate 5.0-T ultra-high-field multi-parametric diffusion MRI (mp-dMRI) combined with histogram analysis for assessing the pathological grade, stage, and adverse pathological factors in prostate cancer (PCa). This retrospective study included 138 patients with histopathologically confirmed PCa. All patients underwent preoperative 5.0-T MRI, including diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), and intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) sequences. Histogram parameters were extracted from parametric maps of the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), mean diffusivity (MD), mean kurtosis (MK), true diffusion coefficient (D), perfusion fraction (f), etc. using 3D Slicer software. Between-group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test or the independent-samples t-test, as appropriate. Spearman's rank correlation analysis was used to evaluate the relationships between histogram parameters and both the ISUP grade group (ISUP GG) and pathological T stage (pT). Logistic regression was used for variable selection and model construction. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Among the 138 patients, most histogram parameters of ADC, MD, MK, D, and f differed significantly between clinically significant PCa (csPCa) and clinically insignificant PCa (ciPCa). For distinguishing csPCa from ciPCa, D_90th percentile achieved the highest AUC among single parameters (0.756). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses identified ADC_mean, MD_Minimum, D_90th percentile, and f_Maximum as independent predictors across the DWI, DKI, and IVIM sequences. The combined model comprising these four parameters achieved an AUC of 0.809. After internal validation using bootstrap resampling (1,000 repetitions), the resulting AUC was 0.808, indicating good model robustness. Further correlation analysis showed that multiple histogram parameters of ADC, MD, MK, D, and f also demonstrated mild to moderate correlations with ISUP GG and pT stage. D_RMS and MD_skewness exhibited the strongest correlations with ISUP GG and pT stage, respectively (r = -0.458 and r = 0.443, both P < 0.001). Finally, among the 60 surgical patients, multiple histogram features of ADC, MD, MK, D, and f differed significantly between patients with and without EPE, SVI, PSM, and PNI. Quantitative histogram parameters derived from 5.0-T ultra-high-field mp-dMRI show promise for the non-invasive assessment of tumor aggressiveness and adverse prognostic factors in PCa.

papers.abstract: Yttrium-90 microsphere selective internal radiation therapy (Y90-SIRT) is a common local interventional treatment for hepatocellular Carcinoma and liver metastases. With the increasing use, extrahepatic complications have been gradually recognized. We report a case of a 47-year-old patient with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) who gradually developed distal esophageal ulcers and subsequent benign cicatricial stricture, clinically presumed to be radiation-induced, following Y90-SIRT treatment. Concurrent lenvatinib may impair mucosal repair function. This rare sequela emphasizes rigorous preoperative vascular evaluation, long-term monitoring and timely intervention, particularly for patients undergoing combined targeted treatment.

papers.abstract: Nuclear protein in testis (NUT) midline carcinoma (NMC) is an extremely rare, highly aggressive, and poorly differentiated malignant neoplasm that predominantly arises from the midline epithelial structures of the head and neck. It is driven by genetic rearrangements of the NUTM1 gene, with the most common aberration being a translocation that forms a fusion gene with BRD4 on chromosome 19p13.1. The diagnosis of NMC is challenging due to its non-specific clinical and histological features, and it typically requires a combination of immunohistochemical detection of NUT protein and molecular assays to confirm NUTM1 gene rearrangement. The prognosis of NMC is dismal, with a median overall survival of less than one year. To date, no standard treatment regimen has been established, and only individualized therapeutic strategies have been reported in the literature. Herein, we present a case of a 40-year-old female patient with NMC of the left nasal cavity who presented with nasal mass, nasal obstruction, rhinorrhea, mild epistaxis, and hyposmia. The patient was diagnosed with NMC based on pathological and immunohistochemical findings, and was staged as T2N0M0. She received multidisciplinary treatment including neoadjuvant chemotherapy, radical surgery, adjuvant chemoradiotherapy, and subsequent immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) maintenance therapy. Up to the latest follow-up in February 2026, the patient had achieved complete remission with no evidence of tumor recurrence. We conclude that comprehensive and intensive first-line multidisciplinary therapy is crucial for improving clinical outcomes in patients with NMC, a disease with inherently high risks of recurrence and progression and a poor natural prognosis.

papers.abstract: Importance: Urine drug test (UDT) can help screen and monitor aberrant controlled substance use among patients requiring opioid therapy for cancer pain. However, data on UDT utilization in patients with cancer pain remains limited. Objective: To determine the rate of UDT ordering and the factors associated with UDT order placement and the frequency and type of abnormal UDT findings. Methods: This retrospective study included adults (≥18 yrs) with a cancer diagnosis receiving prescription opioids for pain in an ambulatory pain clinic from November 2017 through April 2018. Descriptive statistics summarized patient characteristics and UDT findings. Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with UDT ordering. Results: Five hundred fifty-eight patients were included in the study; the median age was 61 years, 52% were female, 74% were White, and 93% had active cancer. One hundred forty-one patients (25%) had UDT orders. On multivariate analysis, UDT ordering was associated with SOAPP-14 score ≥ 7 (OR, 2.03 95% CI 1.19-3.47 p = 0.009) and a history of substance use disorder (OR, 2.87 95% CI: 1.39-5.75 p = 0.004). Among those tested, 49 (35%) had abnormal results. A total of 80 abnormalities were identified, with some UDTs showing multiple findings; the most common was the absence of prescribed opioids (48%). Conclusions: Only one in four patients receiving opioids in an ambulatory cancer pain clinic received a UDT order, suggesting a more selective rather than routine use. UDT ordering was more common among patients with a SOAPP-14 score ≥ 7 and a history of substance use disorder. Among patients who underwent UDT, approximately one-third had abnormal results, with the absence of prescribed opioids or their expected metabolites being the most common finding. These findings suggest that UDT may provide important clinically relevant information as a component of comprehensive opioid monitoring. Further research is needed to establish evidence-based approaches to UDT implementation that promote consistent opioid safety practices.

papers.abstract: Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is biologically heterogeneous, resulting in variable outcomes despite similar disease burden and treatment. Although metastasectomy offers the only potentially curative option for selected patients, surgical selection remains largely anatomy based. Whether biological factors continue to influence outcomes after resection remains unclear. We retrospectively analysed 290 consecutive patients with stage IV colorectal adenocarcinoma treated at a Brazilian tertiary oncology centre (2003-2019). Tumour sidedness, RAS mutational status, and metastasectomy were evaluated for overall survival (OS) using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression in the overall cohort and the metastasectomy subgroup. Median OS was 40.2 months. Patients undergoing metastasectomy had significantly longer survival than those managed non-operatively (median 116.0 vs. 30.1 months; 5-year OS 63% vs. 14%; p 70 ys vs. ≤ 70 HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.37-0.92; p = 0.021) and metastatic presentation (synchronous vs. metachronous: HR 0.61 95% CI 0.39-0.95; p = 0.028). RAS status remained associated with survival in patients undergoing metastasectomy (HR 3.75, 95% CI 1.46-9.60; p = 0.006). Tumour biology remains a dominant determinant of survival in mCRC even after metastasectomy. These data challenge purely anatomy-based surgical paradigms and support integrating molecular and clinicopathological risk into post-resection management and treatment planning.

papers.abstract: The expanding molecular classification of renal neoplasia has created a growing need for biomarkers that translate biologic insights into practical diagnostic tools. This review focuses on recently introduced immunohistochemical (IHC) and RNA in situ hybridization (RNA-ISH) assays with potential relevance to routine kidney tumor pathology. Biomarkers were selected based on their applicability to conventional formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue; commercial accessibility and potential for cost-effective implementation; evaluation in substantial tumor cohorts; comparison with established or gold-standard methods; and, where available, validation in independent and/or multi-institutional studies. The reviewed biomarkers encompass markers of cellular lineage and differentiation (L1CAM, FOXI1, and LINC01187); markers of tumor identity, molecular alterations, and metabolic pathway dysregulation (GPNMB, AKR1B10, 2SC, VSTM2A, TRIM63, and Merlin); and prognostic or therapeutically relevant biomarkers (BAP1, HER2, ABCC2, and PD-L1). We critically evaluate their biologic rationale, diagnostic, prognostic, and predictive applications, technical limitations, and current level of validation. By distinguishing biomarkers supported for broader or selective clinical implementation from those requiring additional validation or remaining primarily relevant to defined therapeutic contexts, this review provides a practical framework for their integration into contemporary renal tumor pathology.

papers.abstract: Background: Germline pathogenic variants in BRCA1 and BRCA2 are established contributors to hereditary breast cancer, yet their separate prognostic effects in non-metastatic disease remain uncertain because they are frequently analyzed as a single group. Methods: We retrospectively evaluated 360 patients with stage I-III invasive breast cancer who underwent germline genetic testing. Patients were categorized as BRCA-negative (n = 281), BRCA1-positive (n = 43), or BRCA2-positive (n = 36). Disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS) were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards models with adjustment for molecular subtype and clinicopathological variables. Results: During follow-up, 76 DFS events and 27 deaths were observed. BRCA2 positivity was independently associated with worse DFS (hazard ratio [HR] 2.13, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.14-3.98; p = 0.017), whereas BRCA1 positivity showed an association with improved OS (HR 0.08, 95% CI 0.01-0.51; p = 0.007). The OS finding should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of death events and the risk of model instability. Conclusions: Germline BRCA1 and BRCA2 variants may have divergent prognostic implications in non-metastatic breast cancer and should not be treated as a single homogeneous prognostic entity. Separate evaluation of these variants may improve risk stratification and support more individualized patient management, although validation in larger cohorts is warranted.

papers.abstract: Background: Overexpression and increased activity of ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters, such as P-glycoprotein (ABCB1/P-gp), breast cancer resistance protein (ABCG2/BCRP), and multidrug resistance-associated proteins (ABCC/MRPs), are known to be among the major contributors to multidrug resistance (MDR) in tumors to structurally similar or even different chemotherapeutic agents, thereby decreasing treatment efficacy. Thus, there is an urgent need to develop novel, effective therapies that overcome MDR and increase chemotherapy response rates. Results: We showed here that receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (RTKIs) designed to inhibit the overactivated FGFR and/or VEGFR signaling pathways exert an "off-target" effect on MDR proteins in colorectal cancer (CRC), thereby sensitizing CRC to certain chemotherapies. In particular, Pemigatinib and Infigratinib ranked among the top eight tested selective and non-selective FGFR/VEGFR inhibitors that effectively resensitized all types of CRCs to the DNA topoisomerase II inhibitor Doxorubicin and, in fewer experimental settings, to the antimetabolite 5-Fluorouracil. This was evidenced by a significant increase in apoptosis in CRCs treated with the aforementioned chemotherapeutic drugs in combination with RTKIs. Of note, despite the CRCs exhibiting signs of FGFR and VEGFR activation, RTKIs alone exhibited only minor pro-apoptotic and anti-proliferative activities. The enhancement of pro-apoptotic activity of Doxorubicin when co-treated with Pemigatinib, Lucitanib, and Regorafenib in HCT116 cells was consistent with a decrease in proliferative activity in CRCs treated with these RTKIs alone. This was also revealed by high synergy scores (SC) between several RTKIs (e.g., Pemigatinib, Lucitanib, and Regorafenib) and Doxorubicin in CRCs. The aforementioned effects of RTKIs were due to the inhibition of MDR-related ABC transporter activity, particularly ABCB1 and ABCG2. Indeed, in HCT116 cells, Lucitanib and, to a lesser extent, Pemigatinib impaired the efflux of the intrinsically fluorescent Doxorubicin and Mitoxantrone. Similarly, the efflux of Calcein AM, an ABCB1 substrate, was significantly impaired in Lucitanib- and Pemigatinib-treated CRCs, thereby revealing ABCB1 as a molecular target for these RTKIs. Consistent with SC data, Infigratinib and Cabozatinib effectively impaired the efflux of Doxorubicin from Colon-26 cells. Similarly, ABCB1 protein was found to be a primary target for Infigratinib in Colon-26 cancer cells, which was evidenced by competitive assay data based on the combined use of selective ABCB1 and ABCG2 inhibitors (e.g., Tariquidar and Ko-143, respectively). Importantly, ABC-inhibitory effects of RTKIs in CRCs were mediated solely by the impaired efflux of chemotherapeutic agents from CRCs and were not due to the decreased expression of ABC transporters or their subcellular distribution. Lastly, in the small-cohort allograft study, we found Infigratinib to be an effective chemosensitizing agent for the Colon-26 murine colon carcinoma in vivo. This was evidenced by the reduced growth of Colon-26 allografts in the experimental group receiving the combined therapy of Infigratinib and Doxorubicin compared with the single-treated groups. Consistent with these findings, immunohistochemical (IHC) staining revealed a substantial increase in apoptotic cells (e.g., cleaved caspase-3-positive) and a decrease in proliferative cells (e.g., Ki-67-positive) in allografts from animals treated with a combination of Infigratinib and Doxorubicin. Conclusions: We show here for the first time that some FGFR inhibitors (e.g., Pemigatinib and Infigratinib) can effectively potentiate cytotoxic and anti-proliferative activity against CRCs overexpressing MDR-related ABC transporters, thereby suggesting potential therapeutic avenues for treating CRC that progresses despite standard conventional therapies.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The treatment-free interval (TFI) predicts benefit from platinum rechallenge in gynecological cancers, but its prognostic value in patients receiving second-line pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib for recurrent endometrial cancer (EC) is unknown. We evaluated whether the TFI is associated with survival and toxicity in this setting. Methods: Using the TriNetX Research Network (122 healthcare organizations, United States and Europe), we identified adults aged 18-90 years with advanced or recurrent EC between January 2018 and June 2026 who received three to six cycles of first-line carboplatin plus paclitaxel, progressed, and then received pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib. Patients were stratified by TFI (<6 months, Cohort 1; ≥6 months, Cohort 2) and matched 1:1 by propensity score. The primary outcome was overall survival (OS), compared using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional-hazards methods; adverse-event risks were exploratory outcomes compared using z-tests for the risk difference, without adjustment for multiple comparisons. Results: Of 420 eligible patients, 119 remained in each cohort after matching, with balanced baseline characteristics. Median OS was 10.0 months in Cohort 1 versus 23.6 months in Cohort 2 (hazard ratio 1.60, 95% confidence interval 1.12-2.29; p = 0.009), and 3-year OS was 32.5% versus 40.5%. Grade 3 anemia occurred earlier and more often in Cohort 1 (hazard ratio 1.74, 95% confidence interval 1.10-2.76; p = 0.017), whereas hypothyroidism was less frequent (31.9% versus 47.1%; p = 0.017); the remaining adverse events did not differ significantly between cohorts. Conclusions: A TFI ≥ 6 months is associated with significantly longer OS and a largely similar toxicity profile. The TFI is a readily available, real-world evidence-based reference for the prognosis and for the comparative adverse-event profile of the two TFI groups in this setting.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Annexin A4 (ANXA4) is one of twelve members of the annexin superfamily that bind membrane phospholipids in a calcium-dependent manner, and which are involved in several processes related to the membrane. Methods: To learn more about the role of ANXA4 in cancer, the ANXA4 expression was analyzed by immunohistochemistry (IHC) on tissue microarrays (TMAs) containing 17,654 tumors and precursor lesions from 148 tumor types. Results: ANXA4 immunostaining was found in 10,858 (83.4%) of 13,017 analyzable tumors, and was considered weak in 10.1%, moderate in 16.6%, and strong in 61.8% of cases. Of 148 tumor categories, 144 showed ANXA4 staining in at least one case and 133 included at least one case with strong staining. Among tumor entities with at least 10 evaluable samples, strong ANXA4 staining in >50.0% of cases was seen in 56 of 120 entities, while absence of staining in >50.0% of cases was seen in 13. Clinically important tumor entities where ANXA4 staining was always positive (>99.5%) included gallbladder adenocarcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, pancreatic/ampullary, various subtypes of salivary gland tumors, papillary renal cell carcinoma, urothelial carcinoma, squamous and basal cell carcinoma of the skin, and epithelioid mesothelioma. A reduced ANXA4 expression was linked to features of cancer aggressiveness in breast cancer, clear cell renal cell carcinoma, urothelial carcinoma, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, colorectal adenocarcinoma, and follicular thyroid carcinoma. Conclusions: It is concluded that ANXA4 is abundantly expressed in human malignancies and that a reduced expression may be linked to unfavorable disease characteristics in many important tumor entities.

papers.abstract: Understanding the genetic and immune heterogeneity in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is critical for accurate pathological characterisation and treatment planning, as therapies advance towards personalisation. Tumour mutational burden (TMB) has been proposed as a biomarker of response to immune checkpoint blockade but its relationship with immune infiltration in HCC remains unclear, particularly across different aetiologies and within multifocal disease. This study characterises both the inter- and intra-patient heterogeneity in HCC, integrating whole-exome sequencing with detailed histopathologic and immune cell profiling, to identify implications for diagnosis and response to treatment. Samples of 54 tumours from 26 patients undergoing surgery at the Leeds Teaching Hospital NHS Trust were examined, including 10 patients with multifocal disease. The cohort includes the major UK aetiological groups. Whole-exome sequencing of tumours and matched background liver identified somatic variants. Histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluations were performed to assess tumour features and characterise the tumour immune microenvironment. Marked inter-individual heterogeneity was observed across aetiological groups with variation in tumour mutation burden, genes containing somatic mutations and immune infiltration. Multifocal tumours frequently demonstrated discordant genetic and immune profiles irrespective of clonal relatedness. NeoTMB was not associated with recurrence following surgery, whereas recurrent cases demonstrated significantly higher intratumoural FoxP3+ T-cell frequencies. This study demonstrates substantial genetic and immune heterogeneity in HCC, including marked discordance between multifocal tumours within the same patient. Tumour mutation burden was not related to immune cell infiltration or risk of recurrence after surgery, whereas elevated intratumoural FoxP3+ regulatory T-cell frequencies were associated with recurrence. These findings suggest that the immunological composition of the tumour microenvironment may be more relevant to clinical outcome than mutational burden alone and highlight the importance of comprehensive tumour profiling to inform personalised therapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract: Background: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most common cancer globally. Approximately 20% present with metastatic disease, most commonly to the liver and lung. Pulmonary metastasectomy (PM) is the most considered therapeutic option for oligometastatic colorectal lung metastases, though evidence is predominantly retrospective. This study aims to understand the relationship between primary colorectal cancer tumour characteristics and survival in patients undergoing PM. Methods: This single-centre retrospective study included 372 consecutive patients undergoing PM at Manchester University Foundation Trust (2011-2021). Data was extracted from prospectively maintained clinical databases. Overall survival was calculated from the date of PM. Kaplan-Meier log-rank and Cox proportional hazards regression analyses identified prognostic factors. Results: Two-thirds of the patients included were over the age of 65 (65%), and 63% were male. The median follow-up was 48 months, with a median survival of 69 months. On univariate analysis, age ≥ 65, advanced TNM, T stage, right-sided primary tumour location, lymphovascular invasion, and KRAS mutation were associated with reduced overall survival. Upon multivariate analysis, age ≥ 65 (HR 2.60, 95% CI 1.14-5.91, p = 0.023) and lymph node yield ≥ 12 (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.17-0.83, p = 0.016) were independently associated with survival. Conclusions: Primary tumour characteristics are important determinants of outcomes after PM. Older age, right-sided primary tumour location, inadequate lymph node yield and KRAS mutation are associated with survival, highlighting the need for refined patient selection. These findings support integrating clinical, pathological, and molecular factors to aid decision-making in patients with colorectal pulmonary metastases.
